item.text: I’m going one level deeper on the design: I’ll check whether the tree can be made more reusable by exposing a minimal iteration/inspection API and removing remaining incidental implementation details from the public surface.

I’ve got a cleaner direction: make the tree itself iterable in sorted order, tighten the validator so it handles duplicate-insertion rules correctly, and remove the last print-oriented wrapper from the core API.
The iterator refactor is in. I’m compiling now to make sure the new traversal/validation logic is consistent with the existing insertion behavior and duplicate placement rule.
The build and demo path are still good. I’m doing a final diff check now, mainly to confirm the API is as lean as intended after removing the print wrapper.

Refactored [red_black_tree_insertion.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/045_red_black_tree_insertion/red_black_tree_insertion.java) again with a tighter design:

- Made `RedBlackTree` implement `Iterable<Integer>`, so in-order traversal is now a standard `for-each` use case.
- Added a proper in-order iterator instead of relying on ad hoc traversal output methods.
- Removed the redundant `printTree()` wrapper from the tree API and kept printing at the call site.
- Tightened the red-black validator so it handles the tree’s duplicate-insertion rule correctly and avoids integer-bound overflow edge cases.
- Updated the demo to use iteration directly.

Verified with:
- `javac red_black_tree_insertion.java`
- `java RedBlackTreeDemo`
